title: Give Him Time

source.title: Trump supporters confront Iran, affordability concerns with a message for critics: 'Give him time'
source.note: published 10-27 06:00 ET (created 10-26 21:08 ET); the 10-27 sweep (matched on 'iran', 'collins', 'midterm', 'house race'). Fox's station on the roster is 'RI?' — proposed, ruling owed; scored as RI on the 10-20/10-21/10-23/10-24 precedents, the Diesel Index's RI seat, flag on the figure. Read in full via the cloud fetch; reductions filed, no quotation over twelve words. A rally page: the article, four voters, a nominee, a spokesperson and the holder, from Perry, Georgia, Saturday 10-24. Chosen over the day's other Fox rally page (Port Huron, Michigan, 10-26 18:00 — the same page with no dollar figure) because this one carries the price with a date and a cause and the holder's own clock; my call

object.label: H1 — the Russian diesel deal (PG01 layer 1): the price leg (H1c) at the pump, read at a rally — Georgia gas $3.66 against $2.72 in February (¶10), the Strait named by the article as the cause (H6 marked), the holder's clock restated at the rally ('oil prices will come down soon', ¶14) and adopted by the voters as patience ('give him time', 'temporarily', 'worth paying'); the gas↔votes predicate from the voters' side

zAxis.pos: prices come down by the deal — soon
zAxis.neg: they do not — the pump is a dollar up on February with the Strait as its cause, and 'soon' is a voter's patience, not a date

transformNote: the shadow is the holder's promise — diesel 'COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST' (10-11), now 'oil prices will come down soon' at a rally (10-24). The page puts the pump beside it ($3.66 vs $2.72, with the Strait as the cause) and lets four voters read the gap: the price is temporary, a cost worth paying, give him time. The deal, the cargo, the waiver and diesel itself are not on the page; the cure's name has dropped out of the holder's sentence and only its clock remains — 'soon', undated, the fourth phrasing of the clock in sixteen days

Forty-one blocks fetched, twenty-six body paragraphs reduced; sixteen scored, one constitutive (Trump @O, the principal, declared z +0.9 — 'come down soon'). Object declared on H1c at the pump with H6 marked (¶10) — the second cut of the day on PG01; chosen over the Port Huron page (10-26) because this one has the price with a date and a cause and the holder's own clock, and over Fox Business 10-26 'Bessent: Iran's economy collapsing' (Operation Economic Outcast; the blockade; filed in the pass from its opening) because that page is the force's finance, not the price. split.note: one station, two planes: the article (the price dated and caused, the holder's number checked against the BLS — 6–16) and the voters (the price as patience, a cost, a thing that would not matter — 30–62). The voters do not disagree with the article's number; they read it as temporary. No migration inside one voice on the page; Barkman moves from 'give him time' (40) to 'full force' (58) but on different objects

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: supporters confront Iran, affordability concerns with a message for critics: give him time — backed him despite $3.66 gas and 36% approval
lines.note: THE DOOR: the dek carries the page's two numbers and the hed carries its clock. 'Give him time' is the shadow's 'soon' in the voter's mouth
lines.zWhy: a price met with 'give him time' is a price not yet down, read as coming

lines.quote: standing by him amid affordability concerns and higher gas prices stemming from the Iran war
lines.note: the thesis; the cause named (the war), not yet the Strait; 'higher' without a figure
lines.zWhy: higher gas prices stemming from the war are a price the deal has not moved

lines.quote: approval 36%, disapproval 64%; Saturday's rally with Jackson, Collins and House candidates
lines.note: the record: the poll and the slate; placement
lines.zWhy: an approval at 36 at the rally is a cure not yet felt by the room outside it

lines.quote: Ossoff by 1.22% in the January 2021 runoff; Trump Georgia by 2.2% in 2024; act as if he is on the ballot November 3
lines.note: the slate's register — two margins and the date; reads neither way on the price
lines.zWhy: two margins and a date read neither way on the pump

lines.quote: people are upset about gas prices and the rest; give him time and they will see improvement
lines.note: THE TITLE: the delivery claim adopted by a voter, with no date — 'time' is the unit. The shadow's clock ('FAST', 10-11; 'soon', 10-24) read as patience
lines.zWhy: a price that needs time is a price read as coming down, later

lines.quote: Georgia gas about $3.66 a gallon against $2.72 in February before the war; Iranian attacks on vessels and threats to Hormuz shipping pushed oil prices up worldwide; Pew: about 65% disapprove of the Iran actions
lines.note: THE PRICE, DATED, WITH ITS CAUSE — H6 MARKED: the pump up 94 cents on February with the Strait as the article's cause ('Iranian attacks', 'threats to Hormuz shipping' — the restrictor named, as AJ named it the same day); the deal is not the cure here because it is not on the page. The page's lowest-Dia line
lines.zWhy: a pump a dollar up on February with the Strait as its cause is a price the deal has not moved

lines.quote: temporarily higher pump prices are worth paying to keep Iran from a nuclear weapon
lines.note: 'temporarily' — the second clock on the page, undated; the price priced against the war's purpose (the 10-26 Port Huron voters' line, 'short term pain for long term gain')
lines.zWhy: a price called temporary is a price read as coming down, undated

lines.quote: most proud of what the president has done in Iran
lines.note: the oscillation zone: the price has left the line for the war; vacancy (the object absent)
lines.zWhy: pride in the war reads the price as the war's, not the deal's

lines.quote: gas prices really wouldn't matter against a nuclear attack on the US
lines.note: the price read out of the line by a larger object — the Protocol's verdict-over-object pattern; vacancy
lines.zWhy: a price that would not matter is a price not read at all

lines.quote: oil prices will come down soon; inflation 1.7% over the past three months
lines.note: constitutive — THE HOLDER'S CLOCK, fourth phrasing: 'COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST' (10-11) → 'immediately' (the 300,000 t) → 'soon' (10-24). The cure's name (Russian diesel, the Strait) has dropped out of the sentence; only the direction and the clock remain. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: the BLS annual CPI was 3.7% in September — a different period from the 1.7% three-month figure
lines.note: THE CHECK: the article sets the record's number beside the holder's and names the difference (period, not rate). The page's lowest-Dia line with ¶10; the Press does not say the holder lied — it says the article measured
lines.zWhy: an inflation checked against the BLS is a cure not yet in the official number

lines.quote: investing in children is significant; Trump will start giving kids financial intelligence
lines.note: off the object (Trump Accounts); vacancy — filed in the pass as a slate sighting
lines.zWhy: a line about children's accounts reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: does not want the country lost; full force for Trump and the Republicans
lines.note: the page's most denominated voter line: 'lost', 'full force' — the price nowhere; vacancy
lines.zWhy: a country not to be lost is a price not in the sentence

lines.quote: the midterms an uphill battle; Trump's backing matters for a candidate he knew less
lines.note: the gas↔votes predicate from the voters' side: 'uphill' is the only line on the page where a supporter reads the vote as at risk
lines.zWhy: an uphill battle at $3.66 is a price read as costing votes, by the side paying

lines.quote: he can't be bought, so his endorsements can be trusted
lines.note: denominated; the endorsement as the object; vacancy
lines.zWhy: a holder who can't be bought reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: Ossoff terrible; Collins the superior candidate if he can get his message out
lines.note: the nominee's frame on the race; vacancy
lines.zWhy: a superior candidate reads neither way on the pump

lines.quote: passed the Laken Riley Act, cut taxes; the only candidate who can beat radical leftist Ossoff; a bipartisan workhorse
lines.note: the page's most denominated line, by the campaign: 'radical leftist', 'workhorse' — the price nowhere; vacancy
